checks.detail: AST comparison at055f9 confirms16 existing functions/classes unchanged, including output_roots, checked_path, source_identity, prepare, stop_gradle, uploaded_evidence_is_retained, android_sdk_binding, android_proc_bytes, android_proc_identity, verify_apple_cleanup and context. checks.area: Narrow privileged command / source and environment
checks.detail: Client accepts only strictly typed/ranged original nonroot UID, PID and starttime; caller real/effective UID must match. Command is fixed /usr/bin/sudo -n -- /usr/bin/python3 -I -S -B plus canonical nonredirected sibling linux_exe_reader.py and decimal UID/PID/start arguments. No shell, caller command/path, inherited Python/import environment, or whole-cleanup sudo. cwd=/; explicit environment only PATH=/usr/bin:/bin and LC_ALL=C before sudo sets caller metadata. Standalone helper imports only stdlib and checks Linux, real/effective root and sudo SUDO_UID exactly equal the original bound UID.
checks.boundary: This is reviewed code in the trusted, source-bound isolated checkout—not an OS-enforced privilege sandbox or immutable-root-owned script deployment. Concurrent malicious mutation of the helper by a compromised runner is outside that trust model; source/control admission and the clean checkout must remain intact. No stronger runtime immutability claim is made.

checks.detail: Helper pins /proc and one decimal PID directory with O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_CLOEXEC|O_NOFOLLOW. Only stat/status records and exe readlink/stat are accessed; no target argv/environment/maps/memory/file payload, process enumeration, target signal, file modification, deletion or executable launch. stat/status opens are directory-relative and no-follow, each capped8192B. Expected starttime and all four original UID values are checked before AND after two exe observations. Path/device/inode/mode must agree; nonregular, nonabsolute, oversized or deleted executable paths fail. FDs close in finally blocks. Outer before/after UID/lifetime and canonical SDK/emulator path/device/inode checks remain authoritative.

Existing4096-entry,8192B-record and5s scan ceilings remain. Parent invocation timeout=min(2s,remaining scan budget), with deadline checked again; privileged helper sets its own1s ITIMER_REAL timer and emits at most65536B. Timer is self-only, not target process control. Client rejects nonzero/timeout/unavailable, oversized/nonbytes/malformed/duplicate-key responses, wrong schema/UID/PID/start, invalid observations, bool/noninteger/out-of-range metadata, nonabsolute/NUL/oversized/deleted paths, nonregular or unequal observations. Fixed error codes/types only; no stdout/stderr/argv/path or raw exception text enters audit receipts. Producer bounds output before write; client size checking is post-capture, not an independent streaming quota.

Original UID selection is done before fallback and never substituted with root UID. Successful partial unprivileged reads are not discarded/retried. Helper failure remains FAIL; helper success does not skip outer identity, SDK binding, own-observer sampling, budget, or emulator-subtree detection. Any SDK/emulator executable observation still fails. Privilege is limited to the fixed exe reader; output traversal/removal stays unprivileged and behind existing stop/source/ownership/upload/audit guards.

All prior hygiene test methods preserved; five added hygiene methods plus ten new helper/client methods,48 methods total across the two modules. Source covers default negative/counters; opt-in first-EACCES-only success; later/EPERM/missing no escalation; outer churn/SDK executable/helper-failure retention; invalid CLI after stop; original caller/SUDO_UID and numeric bounds; pinned dirfd/no-follow records, mixed/changing identity, record/path/response limits, timer/privacy; exact command/env/remaining-timeout and malformed/duplicate/wrong-binding protocol. Helper/client new tests are Linux-scoped mocked/owned-file fixtures, not live sudo/proc proof.

static_validation.ast_parse: All four pinned files parsed with Python stdlib AST; no module import or function execution.
